hypothesis: A conventional trainable key-query/value cross-attention model with explicit structural support-pair access can learn novel key-value associations from the exact information provided to the native hybrid, giving a reliable benchmark positive control. This is task-learnability qualification only; no hybrid-versus-control superiority inference is permitted.
methodological_boundary: The conventional comparator has an explicit content-addressed access prior and far fewer parameters than the 90k hybrid. It is intentionally a strong task-positive baseline, not a compute/parameter matched architectural superiority comparison.

task.distribution: independent Rademacher key/value vectors resampling repeated keys within each episode
task.targets: heldout query value; never present in query token features

baseline.layers: independent trainable linear query/key/value/output maps, learned positive attention-temperature, softmax over only preceding support keys
baseline.input_scope: support keys and values, query key; no query target, no labels during evaluation

stop_conditions: any extra or fewer optimizer steps

reporting.future: If task is learnable, separately freeze a matched-compute fully trained hybrid study; retain the previous eight-step hybrid NULL unchanged. If baseline fails, stop and diagnose the baseline rather than claiming hybrid capability.
